title: Profiler with 'time: Self' includes time from _ready in added scenes
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in 4.7.2. I do remember seeing it before, but I don't have the exact version numbers ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue, 08 Sep 2026 10:22:31 +0000 on Tty - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon Graphics (radeonsi, renoir, ACO, DRM 3.64, 7.2.4-arch1-2) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800H with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 14.95 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description When using "Self" as the time to measure I would expect all things in script functions that take time to be reported exactly once. However, when the function adds a child node to the scene tree then all the time in that node's _ready() function (including time in functions called in _ready) is also being included in the time of the function that adds the node. It looks like the total time of script functions is the sum of all the Self times: the time in this sum also counts the time in the _ready of a newly added node double. #### Example In the above screenshot (from the MRP linked below) the function `add_other` shows a long time. However, all this method do is add a node to the scene tree. The real time is in `busywait`, which is called in the `_ready` method of the added node. This method generates random numbers until 2 seconds have passed. The screenshot also shows the "Script Functions" time being incorrect. It is shown as 4 seconds, while the frame actually only takes 2 seconds. ### Steps to reproduce - Create a method that adds a node to the scene tree - in the _ready method of the node being added (or any method being called directly or indirectly by this _ready method) add some step that takes a long time - In the profiler, look at the frame where the first method is called ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [github.com/jmdejong/godot-profiler-self](https://github.com/jmdejong/godot-profiler-self) Press the button while the profiler is running and look in the profiler at the frame where the button is pressed. This frame is easy to find if you check the "Script Functions" checkbox to show the total duration of that.
